reviewMethod.methodNotesMd: Reviewed the resource-review context, the full ImplementationGuide StructureDefinition report, the supplied R4 maturity context, the resource-review contract, and the fresh-review/rubric guidance. There were no direct behavior findings whose affected resources include `ImplementationGuide`; shared `Resource` and `DomainResource` behavior findings were considered only as background context, not as ImplementationGuide-specific migration drivers. The deterministic aggregate was treated as prior context and compared against the independent resource-level conclusion.

r4Maturity.effectMd: R4 ImplementationGuide is trial-use/FMM 1, so the baseline stability pressure is weak and breaking changes in authoring/package metadata do not automatically deserve standards escalation. That said, ImplementationGuide is the conformance-publication container for IG packages, so changes that affect page publication, resource cataloging, build parameters, or global profile declarations can still be business-critical for publisher and registry workflows.

overall.oneLineConclusion: ImplementationGuide keeps its identity, but real IG publisher/package migrations must handle several targeted model splits and one datatype replacement; low-cost compatibility still matters most for the page source/name split.

reasoning.thesisMd: ImplementationGuide is not removed, replaced, split, or broadly re-based. The R4-to-R6 migration burden is nevertheless real for ordinary IG authoring and package workflows because R6 remodels several local metadata shapes: page source versus published page name, example flag versus profile metadata, manifest example/profile metadata, and build parameter code representation. That makes a targeted resource-level migration program partially unavoidable for serious IG tooling, but it does not make every additional break low-value to avoid.
reasoning.migrationShapeMd: The migration shape is a moderate targeted remodel rather than a major model replacement. Existing R4 instances are most likely to need transforms when they use `definition.page.name[x]`, `definition.resource.example[x]`, `manifest.resource.example[x]`, `definition.parameter.code`, or `global.type` values for R4 resource types that no longer exist in the R6 resource vocabulary. Several other changes are reverse-direction or interpretation issues: `fhirVersion` adds future release codes while retaining R4 codes locally, `definition.resource` becomes less restrictive, and publication metadata semantics shift without changing most JSON names.
reasoning.compatibilityLeverageMd: Because a real IG migration program is already needed for affected publishers, preserving compatibility is somewhat lower leverage than it would be on a mostly unchanged resource. It is not zero leverage. The `definition.page.name[x]` remodel is central to rendered guide output and can require expert decisions about whether an R4 value was source location, published path, or Binary-backed content; preserving a legacy source alias or supplying a clear transition rule would materially reduce risk. By contrast, the example/profile split and primitive-code-to-Coding change are mostly local transforms once the R6 cleanup is accepted.
reasoning.lessBreakingAlternativesMd: The strongest standards-review candidate is a transition-compatible page model: retain the R4 source choice, including `Reference(Binary)`, as a deprecated alias or preserve old source wire names while adding the clearer R6 `name`/`source[x]` separation. That has conflict-rule costs but addresses the only Revisit finding. Deprecated aliases for `example[x]` could also preserve more old instances, but they would duplicate example/profile facts and require reconciliation, so those breaks look proportionate under low FMM. Keeping `parameter.code` primitive would avoid a hard JSON break, but it would trade away the standard, system-qualified Coding representation that appears to be the R6 goal. Widening the R6 resource-type value set with obsolete R4 codes would reduce some `global.type` failures but would undermine release-specific model precision.
reasoning.behaviorImpactMd: No direct OperationDefinition, SearchParameter, or HTTP behavior finding was assigned to ImplementationGuide. Shared Resource/DomainResource behavior findings such as Resource `$meta` removals, `$validate` changes, and shared special search-parameter metadata can affect generic clients operating on ImplementationGuide instances, but they are not ImplementationGuide-specific content-model changes and should be handled in the base Resource/DomainResource or operation/search reviews.
reasoning.comparisonToDeterministicAggregateMd: The deterministic aggregate reached the same broad labels: `Partial` major migration, `moderate-targeted-remodel`, and `preserve-where-low-cost-but-expect-resource-migration`. The independent review agrees with that outcome but gives more qualitative weight to the non-mechanical nature of the page source/name split than the aggregate's count fields suggest. Conversely, it discounts reverse-only and metadata-only findings more strongly for this low-FMM resource than the raw high/medium impact counts might imply.
reasoning.uncertaintyMd: Confidence is high for the computable structure deltas because the R4 and R6 StructureDefinitions were compared directly. Confidence is lower for standards intent, prevalence, and exact terminology migration because official narrative diffs, rendered IG migration guidance, live terminology expansions, and resource-type ConceptMaps were not available locally.

findingConsiderations.title: Page source/name model split removes R4 definition.page.name[x]
findingConsiderations.reasonMd: This is the most important resource-level finding. It is a hard old-valid/new-invalid break, changes generated model properties, removes the R4 Binary reference choice, adds new source choices, and changes the meaning of the required page `name` from source address to published URL. Because page definitions are central to using an ImplementationGuide as a publishing artifact and migration can be lossy or expert-dependent, this remains standards-review-worthy despite FMM 1.

findingConsiderations.title: Build parameter code changed from primitive code to Coding
findingConsiderations.reasonMd: This is a clear hard instance and codegen break because the same `code` property changes from a JSON string to a Coding object. It helps drive the conclusion that a targeted IG migration program is needed. However, the known HL7 parameter code list is unchanged and the R6 goal of system-qualified, tool-specific parameters is coherent, so this is mainly a migration chore rather than a low-cost compatibility preservation candidate.

findingConsiderations.title: Definition resource example[x] split into isExample and profile
findingConsiderations.reasonMd: R4 `exampleBoolean` and `exampleCanonical` are invalid in R6 and generated models must change. The forward mapping is usually straightforward, while the R6 model more clearly separates example status from one-or-more profile assertions. Deprecated aliases would preserve old JSON but create duplicate representations and conflict rules, so this is important migration work but not a primary reason to resist the R6 remodel.

findingConsiderations.title: Manifest resource example[x] split into isExample and profile
findingConsiderations.reasonMd: The manifest-side split matters because package manifest consumers may encounter it even if they do not author IG definitions. It mirrors the definition-resource split and should be handled in the same transform. Its compatibility concern is real but local once the clearer `isExample`/`profile` model is accepted.

findingConsiderations.title: Global resource type binding tracks the R6 resource set and excludes many R4 type codes
findingConsiderations.reasonMd: This is a potential hard break for R4 IGs that declare global profiles on resource types removed, renamed, or consolidated before R6. It can affect validation assumptions across an IG, so it needs explicit migration mapping or ConceptMap support. It does not by itself argue for keeping obsolete resource-type codes in the R6 base value set, because `global.type` should identify current R6 resource types.

findingConsiderations.title: Publication metadata definitions shifted semantics without changing JSON shape
findingConsiderations.reasonMd: The same metadata fields can now answer different governance questions, such as last significant change versus publication date and maintainer jurisdiction versus intended-use jurisdiction. This can affect registries and package governance, but it is not a structural R4-to-R6 validation break. Under FMM 1 it belongs in migration guidance and business-rule review rather than driving a stronger resource-level compatibility conclusion.

findingConsiderations.title: FHIR-version binding adds R5/R6 and ballot codes that are not R4-representable
findingConsiderations.reasonMd: The local comparison found R4 FHIR-version codes retained in R6, so this is not an R4-to-R6 old-valid/new-invalid break. New R6 and ballot codes create expected R6-to-R4 down-conversion loss, which needs converter policy but should not be counted as an avoidable R6 compatibility break for existing R4 IGs.

findingConsiderations.title: Definition.resource minimum cardinality decreased, allowing R6 definitions without resources
findingConsiderations.reasonMd: Lowering the minimum from 1 to 0 cannot invalidate an R4 instance in R6. It only creates a possible R6-to-R4 representability issue for resource-less R6 definitions, so it does not materially shape the forward migration conclusion.

findingConsiderations.title: Resource $meta-add is removed from R6 core
findingConsiderations.reasonMd: Generic clients might use Resource metadata operations against ImplementationGuide instances, and this shared operation removal is important at the Resource behavior level. It is not assigned directly to ImplementationGuide and does not change the ImplementationGuide StructureDefinition migration shape.

findingConsiderations.title: R6 invocation matrix changes instance-level Resource $validate request semantics
findingConsiderations.reasonMd: ImplementationGuide validators may encounter this generic Resource operation behavior, but it is shared Resource-level API surface. It should inform generic tooling migration without being scored as an ImplementationGuide-specific break.

findingConsiderations.title: Core special/profile search parameters changed type metadata for _content, _text, _query, and _profile
findingConsiderations.reasonMd: Shared search-parameter metadata can affect generated clients for any resource, including ImplementationGuide, but the affected resources are Resource and DomainResource. It is background context rather than evidence of local ImplementationGuide remodel.

recommendedNextActions.actionMd: Revisit the `definition.page.name[x]` to `name` plus `source[x]` transition. Consider retaining the R4 source choice as a deprecated alias for one release, or publish explicit normative migration rules for `nameUrl`, `nameReference`, generated pages, and Binary-backed source content.

Publish and test a focused ImplementationGuide R4-to-R6 transform covering page source/name separation, definition and manifest `example[x]` to `isExample`/`profile`, and primitive `definition.parameter.code` to Coding with the standard guide-parameter-code system where applicable.
Provide release-aware guidance or a ConceptMap for `global.type` resource-code migration, especially for removed, renamed, or consolidated R4 resource types used by global profile declarations.

Document metadata interpretation changes for IG registries and publishers, including publication date versus last significant change, intended-use jurisdiction versus maintaining-authority jurisdiction, and when to preserve R4 meanings in extensions or `useContext`.

caveats: No direct ImplementationGuide behavior/API findings were present; shared Resource/DomainResource behavior findings were considered only as context.
The supplied inputs did not include official R4-to-R6 ImplementationGuide narrative diffs, committee rationale, or rendered migration guidance.
Terminology conclusions rely on local ValueSet/CodeSystem comparisons rather than live terminology-server expansions.
No official ConceptMap was available for resource-type codes removed, renamed, or consolidated between R4 and R6.
The R6 input package is a ballot build, so final R6 artifacts may change.
